title: an H2 line inside a thread's Objective or Context breaks the cover read-back: a false CoverEditNotCarried refusal, and sync --to-store would split the field
body: Found in Gtools on 2026-09-26 under v3.2.3: `intent st attach ST0011 design.md --from <file>` refused with CoverEditNotCarried, although intent/st/ST0011/info.md was byte-identical to the render committed at cfd82e5 and no thread.set followed it. ST0011's stored Context (5131 chars) carries its own H2 line, `## Started, P0 (hv, 25 Sep 2026)`. The render places it inside the cover's `## Context`, and the read-back that views::carriable_cover asks (the guard at facade.rs, issue 0559's) splits sections at every H2, so the carried Context is only the text before that line. carried.context != thread.context, so the guard reports a hand edit that nobody made. The remedy it names, `intent sync --to-store ST0011`, would go through the same read-back and truncate the store's Context at that heading, moving the rest. So the remedy misdirects into a content change. Measured read-only: the store opened with ?immutable=1, canon json, git log. Fix direction: either the render escapes or demotes an H2 inside Objective and Context, or the read-back bounds each authored section by the renderer's known next section rather than by any H2; and a round-trip arm for a field that contains a heading. Workaround given to gtools-vc: re-set the Context with the inner heading demoted to H3.
